activity_context.topic_title: The Pythagorean Theorem and the Triangle Inequality

feedback.problem: If $|u\cdot v|+‖u+v‖=12\sqrt{3}$ and $‖v‖=2\sqrt{3}$, then what is the smallest possible value of $‖u‖?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, simplifying, and substituting in the given information, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}12\sqrt{3} & =|u\cdot v|+‖u+v‖ \\  & \le ‖u‖\cdot ‖v‖+‖u+v‖ \\  & =‖u‖\cdot (2\sqrt{3})+‖u+v‖ \\  & =2\sqrt{3}‖u‖+‖u+v‖.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, using the triangle inequality, simplifying, and substituting in the given information, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{3}‖u‖+‖u+v‖ & \le 2\sqrt{3}‖u‖+(‖u‖+‖v‖) \\  & =2\sqrt{3}‖u‖+(‖u‖+2\sqrt{3}) \\  & =(2\sqrt{3}+1)‖u‖+2\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Combining the two inequalities, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}12\sqrt{3} & \le (2\sqrt{3}+1)‖u‖+2\sqrt{3} \\ 10\sqrt{3} & \le (2\sqrt{3}+1)‖u‖ \\ \frac{10\sqrt{3}}{2\sqrt{3}+1} & \le ‖u‖.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the smallest possible value of $‖u‖$ is $\frac{10\sqrt{3}}{2\sqrt{3}+1}.$
